html:
Da Nang in 2026 welcomes travelers with its vibrant energy and a harmonious blend of majestic nature and modern architecture. This article takes you on a journey to explore the city’s must-visit destinations from the lush Son Tra Peninsula and iconic bridges to the timeless charm of Hoi An Ancient Town along with memorable culinary experiences and convenient transportation options.

Located in central Vietnam, Da Nang has long been a favorite destination for both domestic and international travelers thanks to its beautiful beaches, spectacular landscapes, and distinctive architectural landmarks. Beyond its long stretches of white sand and turquoise waters, the city boasts a rich collection of natural attractions, cultural heritage sites, and historical landmarks. From green mountains and symbolic bridges to tranquil ancient streets, every corner of Da Nang tells its own story. This guide offers an in-depth look at the city’s highlights, including the latest travel updates for 2026.

1. Son Tra Peninsula – The Green Gem Of Da Nang

Known as the “green mountain” of Da Nang, Son Tra Peninsula is a breathtaking natural sanctuary featuring dramatic mountains, pristine beaches, and a rich biodiversity. Often referred to as the city’s “green lung,” it is also a protected nature reserve and home to the rare red-shanked douc langur one of the world’s most endangered primates, admired for its striking appearance. The best times to spot these animals are early morning or late afternoon.

One of the peninsula’s highlights is Linh Ung Pagoda at Bai But, home to the 67-meter-tall Lady Buddha statue facing the East Sea. From here, visitors can enjoy panoramic views of Da Nang city, My Khe Beach, and the distant Cham Islands. Ban Co Peak is another popular stop, offering fresh mountain air and sweeping views of both sea and forest. Adventure seekers can enjoy trekking, snorkeling, or relaxing at secluded beaches such as Bai Rang and Bai But. The ideal time to explore Son Tra is during the dry season, from March to September.

2. Da Nang Beaches – A Tropical Paradise

Da Nang is famous for its stunning coastline, with My Khe Beach standing out as the most iconic. Recognized by Forbes as one of the world’s most attractive beaches and praised by Lonely Planet for water sports, My Khe offers soft white sand, crystal-clear water, and a refreshing sea breeze. Visitors can swim, surf, parasail, or simply relax while enjoying fresh seafood at beachfront restaurants.

Other notable beaches include Non Nuoc Beach near the Marble Mountains, Thanh Binh Beach close to the city center, and Pham Van Dong Beach, popular among locals. These beaches are perfect for sunrise and sunset views and offer a peaceful escape from the city’s bustle.

3. Hoi An Ancient Town – Timeless Beauty And Cultural Heritage

Located less than 30 kilometers from Da Nang, Hoi An Ancient Town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site renowned for its well-preserved architecture and multicultural influences from Vietnam, Japan, China, and Europe. Moss-covered rooftops, narrow stone-paved alleys, and colorful lanterns create a romantic and nostalgic atmosphere.

Visitors can explore iconic landmarks such as the Japanese Covered Bridge, Fujian Assembly Hall, and Tan Ky Ancient House. Cultural experiences include lantern-making workshops, traditional tailoring, and cooking classes. At night, Hoi An becomes magical as lanterns illuminate the streets and boats carrying floating candles glide along the Hoai River.

4. Golden Bridge – A Masterpiece In The Clouds

Located within the Sun World Ba Na Hills complex, the Golden Bridge is one of Da Nang’s most iconic landmarks. Supported by two giant stone hands emerging from the mountainside, the golden walkway appears to float above the clouds. Since its opening in 2018, the bridge has gained global recognition and become a symbol of Vietnamese tourism.

Walking across the bridge offers breathtaking views of the Ba Na Mountains and the distant coastline. For the best experience, visit early in the morning or on weekdays to avoid crowds.

5. Han River Swing Bridge – A Symbol Of Innovation

The Han River Swing Bridge is the only swing bridge in Vietnam and a source of pride for Da Nang residents. Designed and built by Vietnamese engineers, the bridge rotates 90 degrees at night to allow ships to pass. This unique event usually takes place late at night and attracts both locals and visitors.

Watching the bridge rotate from a river cruise or a riverside café is a memorable experience and highlights the city’s creativity and modern spirit.

6. Dragon Bridge – Fire And Water Spectacle

Dragon Bridge is one of Da Nang’s most recognizable symbols. Designed in the shape of a dragon inspired by the Ly Dynasty, the bridge represents power and prosperity. Every Saturday and Sunday evening at 9:00 PM, the dragon breathes fire and sprays water, drawing large crowds and creating an unforgettable spectacle.

7. Linh Ung Pagoda – Where Spirituality Meets Nature

Linh Ung Pagoda on Son Tra Peninsula is one of three Linh Ung pagodas forming a spiritual triangle that protects the city. Nestled between the mountains and the sea, the pagoda offers a serene atmosphere and panoramic views. The towering Lady Buddha statue is the tallest of its kind in Vietnam and a symbol of peace and compassion.

8. Marble Mountains – A Sacred Natural Complex

The Marble Mountains, located about 8 kilometers from the city center, consist of five limestone hills named after the five elements. Thuy Son, the largest mountain, features impressive caves, ancient pagodas, and viewpoints overlooking the coast. At the base lies the Non Nuoc Stone Carving Village, famous for its traditional marble sculptures.

9. Da Nang Museum Of Cham Sculpture – A Gateway To Ancient Civilization

Established in 1915, the Museum of Cham Sculpture houses the world’s largest collection of Cham artifacts. With nearly 2,000 exhibits dating from the 5th to the 15th century, the museum offers deep insight into the art, religion, and culture of the ancient Champa Kingdom.

10. Asia Park – A World Of Colorful Entertainment

Asia Park is a modern amusement complex featuring thrilling rides, family-friendly attractions, and a cultural zone representing ten Asian countries. The highlight is the Sun Wheel, a 115-meter-tall Ferris wheel offering stunning nighttime views of Da Nang.

11. Da Nang Cuisine – A Journey Of Flavors

Da Nang is a culinary paradise where travelers can enjoy local specialties such as Mi Quang, fish cake noodle soup, banh xeo, nem lui, and Nam O fish salad. Street food markets and seaside eateries offer authentic flavors at affordable prices, making food exploration an essential part of any visit.

12. Transportation In Da Nang

Getting around Da Nang is easy and convenient. Motorbike rentals are popular for independent exploration, while taxis and ride-hailing services offer comfort and safety. Public buses provide a budget-friendly option for traveling between major attractions.

With its stunning landscapes, rich cultural heritage, modern infrastructure, and welcoming atmosphere, Da Nang is more than just a tourist destination it is a city full of inspiration. Whether you are a nature lover, a history enthusiast, or simply looking for relaxation, Da Nang promises unforgettable experiences and lasting memories.
